Comments: This well was drilled in a forested area off of Point View Road in March 2006. The response also states that the excavation will be left open until the attainment of standards from the Alternative Remediation Process has been demonstrated. The violations at the site can be closed when the contaminated soil has been replaced, the site has been graded to final contours, and the manifest and tipping information for soil disposal has been received by the Department.

SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2/07/2023
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 984688
Permit API: 081-21879
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/07/2023
Comments: This inspection was conducted in order to assess conditions Pad B after the a notification from the operator that additional fluid with elevated electrical conductivity (EC) was discovered once rig mats were removed from the dancefloor on the pad. The operator stated in their notification that they believed that this fluid could be associated with the reported produced fluid release from 2/3/23. Two snubbing units are in operation on Pad B. I met with EQT representative Zac Subra upon arriving on the pad. He first showed me the area where rig mats and timber mats had been removed from a portion of the dancefloor. He stated that they couldn't remove any more of the rig mats and timber mats until the snubbing units finished the drill out because the flare stack was sitting on the dancefloor. The fluid present in the area of the removed rig mats had an EC between 3.45 mS/cm toward the southern end and >19.99 mS/cm at the northern end. Mr. Subra said that the clam shell boxes had been placed on this area of the dancefloor which they believed had released elevated EC fluid to this area of the pad. He stated that it is against EQT policy to stage the boxes on the well pad without secondary containment but that a contractor had done so anyway.A crew was excavating this area during this inspection. The roll-off box that they were placing the excavated material in was sitting on the rig mats to the west of the uncovered area but did not have any kind of secondary containment underneath it. The Department recommends adding secondary containment at least underneath the end of the roll-off box that has the door on it. In inspection report number 3492854, the Department noted the presence of a roll-box present on the dancefloor without secondary containment and the Department made the recommendation to place the box onto secondary containment.Next, Mr. Subra and I looked at the area on the east side of Pad B where fluid with elevated EC was found the day prior on 2/6/23. A crew was excavating this area as well during this inspection. The crew was placing the impacted pad material into an unlined roll-off box with a door on one end of the box. There was no secondary containment underneath any portion of the box and the box was visibly leaking fluid from the bottom of the door. I showed this to Mr. Subra and he stated that he thought it was melting ice. I recommended that the box be placed onto secondary containment regardless. He then stated that secondary containment could not be constructed for the box due to logistical constraints. I recommended that at a minimum a duckpond or tray of some sort be placed underneath door of the box. The EC of the fluid present in the area where sample 0718-203 was taken the day before was 15.95 mS/cm.I returned to the northwest area of the well pad and took sample 0718-204 from the fluid present where the rig mats and timber mats from the dancefloor had been removed. The sample was sent to the state laboratory the next day to be analyzed for SAC 942 plus Br, Li, and Al.Violations remain outstanding for the produced fluid release to Pad B from the clam shell boxes.

Comments: This inspection was conducted as a follow-up to the release which occurred on 6/24/22. EQT held a safety meeting during my visit to the pad and many EQT representatives were present including Mark Barbier and Rick Hall as well as DCNR representatives Dale Weaver and Rich Glinski. Rick Hall accompanied me on my inspection after the meeting. Equipment for the frac is still staged on the pad but the frac was shut down during this inspection due to the safety meeting. The site was more dry during this inspection than it was during the inspection on the previous day. According to Mr. Hall, vacuum trucks have been vacuuming up fluid from the pad surface. The north edge of the pad surface along the secondary containment for the working tanks, near the blender where the 6/24/22 release occurred, is still damp. Comments: On May 19, 2020, I conducted an inspection of the Vivian Harbison well site in Nottingham Township, Washington County. The inspection was a follow up inspection conducted in response to a fluid release reported to the Department on May 13, 2020 (See SAIR 3033281). The following was observed: Five roll off disposal boxes were staged on the well pad(photo#1). The disposal boxes were labeled as non-hazardous waste with a comment including stone and produced water (photo #2). The impacted area was surrounded with yellow caution tape. The impacted area appeared to be approximately 30' wide and 50' in length. Well pad material (stone) had been removed to an approximate depth of 3.5'. The impacted area stretches along the backside of multiple GPUs. The GPUs did not appear to be equipped with secondary containment. The GPUs appeared to be placed on a series of steel plates. The individual plates did not appear to be welded together (photo #3). I utilized a Field Scout Direct Soil EC meter to collect conductivity readings in and around the impacted area and between the GPUs. The following readings were collected. Behind GPU 592605A, I collected a reading of 8.18 mS under the steel plate (photo#4). I observed a puddle of fluid on the steel plate between GPU 592604A and 592605A, I collected a reading of 12.95 mS. The area was covered with what appeared to be wood chips. I detected conductivity in excess of the reading limit of the unit within the wood chip area the result was Or. The maximum limit of the unit is 20 mS. (photo #5,6,9,10,11, and 12) At GPU 592603A, I collected a reading of 7.51 mS (photo #7 and 8). Based on the observations made during this inspection it does not appear that the Operator has removed the impacted material from the well pad. The GPUs are not equipped with secondary containment and the GPUs may need to be removed to accomplish remediation activity. Violations remain outstanding and new violations are being issued based on the observations made during this inspection.

Comments: Incident Inspection of Expand's "Oil Can" Marcellus well site.Steve Moyer (Expand) called the DEP on Monday (Preisdents Day) February 16, 2026 to report an estimated 30 gallon release of produced liquid (brine) from a tank battery. Moyer explained that a vac truck was filling a 500 barrel tank with brine and it overflowed into secondary liner containment. Approximately 3 gallons of the brine splashed onto the pad surface, and a liner breach leaked some of the brine onto the pad surface. The brine is stored on this pad for hydraulically fracturing Marcellus wells at other Expand sites. Expand removed 4 of the 500 barrel tanks February 18-19 to expose the impacted pad surface for excavation.I spoke with Dakota Manning (Crescent Environmental) on site. He explained they are removing liquid from snow melt that is flowing into the excavated area. They plan to obtain soil samples to comply with Act 2 after the melt liquid stops flowing into the sump. Crescent got electrical conductivity readings of 0.6-1.0 mS/cm from the liquid in the sump.Violations for the brine release are cited to the 015-21874 permit.Cannot assess soil stabilization because ~6 of snow cover. I did not see accelerated erosion or sedimentation.Containment structures are intact. I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies.There is snow in all 3 Marcellus cellars.Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed.Pooled liquid on the pad surface has electrical conductivity of 0.15-0.33 mS/cm with an Oakton PCTS5.Air temp 24FJLP

Violation ID: 8284100
Permit API: 123-49194
Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/03/2026
Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted to document a field review of the recent removal of grub material previously located between the proposed Akins #3 and Akins #4 well pads. William Cenk and Brian Bennett of Trinity Mineral Partners (TMP) were present for the duration of this inspection. Brian Ayers (WQSS) and I, Mathew Haemer (WQS), were present to represent the Department.During the 07/21/26 JPA pre-application meeting between TMP and the Department, Department Technical Services staff requested that the grub material placed south of the roadway between the Akins #3 and Akins #4 well pads be removed as soon as possible to potentially restore the hydrology near the road and well pad construction back to its original condition. It was observed that the grub material had impeded and redirected the flow of an Unnamed Tributary to Jackson Run and had begun to cause E and S problems alongside the roadway, well pad, and below the well pad for the proposed Akins #4 conventional well.At the time of this inspection, it appeared that all of the grub material had been removed as requested. However, TMP had also elected to redefine one of the stream channels below the well pad for Akins #3 and direct its flow through the disturbed area south of the roadway to Akins #4. The excavation work related to this stream channel continues to cause erosion and sedimentation to occur alongside the roadway and well pad for the proposed Akins #4. This is not the outcome Technical Services staff intended to result from the removal of the grub material. At the time of this inspection, the newly excavated stream channel is unprotected from erosion. There are three filter socks installed south of the Akins #4 well pad beyond the excavated stream channel directly in line with this channelized flow. Filter sock is not designed to be installed in channelized flow. All three filter socks are being undercut by the channelized flow. Evidence of erosion and sedimentation is still present before and after each filter sock. The area south and continuing west of Akins #4 that is now accepting the flow of this stream water is beginning to erode. A forested wetland is located west and down grade from the Akins #4 well pad. Bank erosion and saturated earth below the wetland indicate that the stream water overflows the wetland during storm events.The Department has yet to receive an updated E and S Plan that meets the expectations of the Technical Services staff. It is recommended that no further earth disturbance occurs without notification to and approval by the Department.The encroachment violations and violations relating to erosion and sediment control continue in the present condition of this construction and related excavation work.The violation for failure to post the well permit during construction has been closed.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 1/10/2024 to RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC in Cogan House Township, Lycoming county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 1/10/2024
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8171035
Permit API: 081-21912
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cogan House Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 1/10/2024
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator of a release of produced fluid to the pad surface on 1/8/24. The operator reported that the release of produced fluid occurred in a path from the frac tank battery to the production tanks on the well pad when a driver who had already off-loaded produced fluid from the production tanks into the frac tanks left the valve open on the truck which allowed an estimated half barrel of residual produced fluid to leak onto the pad surface when he drove back to the production tanks. The site was covered with snow, slush, and puddles of stormwater during this inspection. I met with Kirby Steck of Range upon arriving on location. He showed me the path where a water truck driver released an estimated half barrel of produced fluid. I conducted screening of the fluid on the well pad between the production tanks and the frac tanks. Near the production tanks, in the offloading area, a puddle of fluid was present beneath a water truck that was emptying the production tanks. The electrical conductivity (EC) of the fluid on the puddle was 5.99 mS/cm. Between the production tanks and the frac tanks, the EC readings were below 2 mS/cm. In a puddle near the frac tank battery, the EC was 2.30 mS/cm. A vacuum truck was also on location sucking up fluid from the pad surface. According to Mr. Steck, the plan was to continue sucking up fluid from the well pad that day and the following day, 1/11/24, and to have a crew come on 1/11/24 to begin excavation on the well pad. Mr. Steck said that the estimated volume of the release was changed to half a barrel after speaking with the trucking contractor who said that the truck had already off-loaded the fluid from the truck at the time that the release occurred. The Department recommends continuing to vacuum up the fluid with elevated electrical conductivity on the pad and to excavate the impacted pad material. Violations noted. Violations remain outstanding for previous releases on the pad.

Comments: This Inspection is being conducted in response to a complaint that was received by the Department on 12/11/2019 regarding concerns about large rusted holes in the sides of several brine tanks. WQS Eric Norman is assisting. The conditions during this inspection are cloudy in the mid 50's. An Act 9 Sign is at the entrance but is very faded. The Department recommends that the Operator maintain the sign to regulated specifications. The ERP and SDS are on site, the ERP appears to be site specific. The access road appears to be built, with no visible signs of accelerated erosion or sedimentation. The well head is labeled. No leaks or discharges observed. The site appears to be constructed and the well appears equipped for production. Associated production equipment and Production Tanks are on site. The Production Tanks are in an earthen dike. The earthen dike appears to have some holes, possibly associated with nuisance wildlife, the Department recommends that the operator take steps to correct those issues in order to maintain the structural integrity of the earthen dike. The Production Tanks appear to be in poor condition with large holes in both tanks toward the top of both. The Tank closest to the well head appears to have corrosion over most of the tank. No leaks, spills, or distressed vegetation is observed. Inspections 2716702, 2819306, and 2856714 mentioned issues with corrosion and holes in these brine tanks dating back to 04/10/2018. The Department is requesting monthly inspection logs for the Production Tanks from 04/10/2018 until 12/30/2019. The Department is also requesting a time table for correcting or removing these tanks. Based on this inspection, violations are being issued. More violations may be issued based on operator response to the NOV's.

Inspection Date: 2020-03-10
Comments: The DEP conducted an incident response inspection of Repsol's DCNR 594 (02-207) well site located in Bloss and Hamilton Townships, Tioga County on 3/10/2020 at 1225 hours. The weather was 50 degrees with an overcast and rain. Ernie Shumbat represented Repsol onsite and oversaw excavation activities. Bishop Brothers Construction handled the excavation activities and Golder (environmental consultant) handled the environmental side of things. Repsol reported that a water truck had released approximately 20 gallons of produced water from a valve to the pad surface in front of the produced water offload area. The release had impacted the pad material directly in front of the offload area (see photo #3). Golder had tested the pad material for electrical conductivity (EC) and marked the area of impact. While I was onsite, Repsol was still waiting for an 811 call approval for excavation. While awaiting approval, excavation as deep as 12 inches was initiated. Impacted material was scraped up and placed in a lined roll-off container for disposal. Areas after the initial scrape were returned to normal soil EC readings (less than 1.0 mS/cm). The small area directly in front of the offload area (believed to absorb most of the release) was still reading high EC. I left the site around 1340 hours and rain had already began falling. Further excavation was conducted and a reported 7 yards of material was removed from the pad and placed in the roll-off container. Photos were provided by Repsol to show the completed excavation area. The area was backfilled and Repsol was awaiting disposal approval to properly dispose of the impacted material. Due to the observations made during the inspection and the timely response made by the operator, violations of the following were noted as immediately corrected against API # 117-22006: 35 P.S. 691.402(b) 35 P.S. 6018.301 25 Pa. Code 78a.57(a)

Comments: This administrative inspection report is in response to the receipt of analytical results for sample number 4406-019 collected on 7/18/2024 at 11:57 AM as part of inspection report #3798130 at the Tract 726 D Pad. Elevated levels of metals and chlorides in the sample analysis indicate a release of a pollutional substance.Sample 4406-019 indicated elevated concentrations of the following parameters: Aluminum - 1.6 mg/L; Barium - 11.0 mg/L; Strontium- 1.44 mg/L; Specific Conductivity- >3,230 micro-ohms/cm; Total Chloride- 600.6 mg/L (photos 1 and 2). PGE submitted an NOV response letter to the Department on August 2, 2024 which stated the following actions were taken regarding the Department's 7/18/2024 inspection: "PGE had a vac truck take up the puddled fluid immediately. A 50 X 15 X > 3 deep area of soil was then dug up and loaded into a lined roll off for sampling and disposal. PGE asserts that it was not in violation of any state or federal regulation nor was PGE acting contrary to the permit issued under the authority of the Department. It cannot be established that the puddled fluid was caused solely by any activity conducted by PGE rather than a combination of mat washing and heavy rainfall."In follow-up inspection #3801042, the Department verified that impacted material was being scraped from the site and placed into a lined rolloff container for sampling. As the volume of pollutional material released to the pad surface has not been measured or quantified, the Department recommends PGE pursue Act 2 remediation response in accordance with 78a.66. Violations noted.

Report Details

Violation ID: 8271850

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 4/20/2026
Comments: On 4/20/2026, the Department conducted an inspection in response to a spill at Minton William well pad in Independence Township, Beaver County. The spill reportedly occurred on 3/31/2026, at 4:15 PM. The spill was reportedly caused when a minor surge of gas caused produced water to release from the casing of well 11H to the graveled well pad, while the operator conducted work on well 11H. An estimated 10 gallons of produced water released and was contained to the graveled well pad. The operator reportedly remediated this release in accordance with 78a.66(c)(1). The operator reported the spill to the Department on 3/31/2026, at 5:11 PM (IR 4172810). Accompanying the Department during this inspection is Range Resources representative Nate Smiell. Intermittently present was Range Resources representative Derek Zofchak. The Erosion and Sedimentation Control General Permit (ESCGP) for this site was terminated on 10/13/2021.The following was observed during the inspection:The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (photo 1). The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan, and new well permits are on site (photos 10-13). The ERP and PPC plan appear to contain the sections required by 78a.55. Eight gas wells are onsite that appear to be equipped for production (photo 16). Well 11H is temporarily shut-in to accommodate the drill rig (photo 18). Smiell reported that well 13H is being drilled at the time of inspection (photo 8). The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment appear to be sound at the time of inspection (photo 4). The GPU/Vertical Separator Units are equipped with interconnected secondary containment drip pans (photos 5 and 6). This form of GPU secondary containment was approved by the Department for use on 6/21/2022. All other storage containers and machinery on site that appear to contain regulated substances are placed within secondary containment (photos 9 and 14). The secondary containments on site appear to be in good condition at the time of inspection, with no observable holes or tears. No evidence of fluid releases, such as staining, was observed on the well pad surface during this inspection. The containment inspection log is available on site in the company trailer (photo 17). The access road and well pad appear to be stable at the time of inspection with no observable concerns relating to accelerated erosion and sedimentation (photos 2 and 3).Based on observations from this inspection, violations shall be noted and immediately corrected against the 3/31/2026 spill.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 5/14/2026 to TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC in Sugar Grove Township, Warren county. 102.4(d) - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS – Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to obtain other necessary permits and authorizations from the Department or conservation district, related to the earth disturbance activity, before commencing the earth disturbance activity, including the well permit.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/14/2026
Violation Code: 102.4(d) - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS – Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to obtain other necessary permits and authorizations from the Department or conservation district, related to the earth disturbance activity, before commencing the earth disturbance activity, including the well permit.
Violation ID: 8275339
Permit API: 123-49194
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/14/2026
Comments: This inspection was conducted to evaluate the status of violations issued on 9/18/2025 and 4/17/2026 associated with the construction of the well site for this proposed conventional well and the access road leading to it. Since the 4/17/2026 inspection, Trinity Mineral Partners (TMP) submitted multiple versions of an updated E and S plan that included additional BMPs and methods to stabilize all disturbed areas. At the time of this inspection, the latest version of the updated E and S plan has not yet met the expectations of the Department's Technical Services staff, as was indicated in a 5/11/2026 email to William Cenk.Throughout this inspection, we observed that a majority of the practices prescribed in the latest version of the updated E and S plan have been implemented. Inlet/outlet rock protection was placed at the installed culverts, rock filters placed in the roadside ditch in the vicinity of the well site for proposed Well # 3, and a combination of erosion blankets and mulch was applied to temporarily stabilize most of the disturbed areas. TMP indicated that seed was applied prior to mulching/placement of the erosion blanket. Erosion blanket was missing upslope of Culvert 1 and there was no evidence of hydro-seeding. The placement of grubbing material along the southern side of the access road that has displaced stream flow continues to result in accelerated erosion and washout along the southern edge of the road and perimeter of the well site for proposed Well # 4.The Department suggests the removal of the stockpile material from approximately the outlet location of Culvert 3 westerly to the newly established point of concentrated flow. Currently, it appears the streamflow is obstructed and migrated towards the pad/access road creating concentrated flow which cannot be stabilized. Without proper stabilization, the additional flow due to the construction activity appears to be causing accelerated erosion and sedimentation to Wetland G. The removal of the waste areas would potentially allow the flow to migrate back to its original drainage path and allow for successful installation of temporary stabilization BMPs, per plan. Department staff can be available for consultation/direction during the removal operation. Waste areas are not to be discarded in other floodways or wetlands. After the submission of the updated and complete E and S plan to Brian Ayers (brayers@pa.gov), temporary stabilization shall be finished. A follow up inspection will be conducted following the completion of the temporary stabilization. A preapplication meeting must be submitted/scheduled before June 15, 2026 in order to address any outstanding violations.Violations that were cited in the 9/18/2025 and 4/17/2026 inspection reports remain unaddressed.The following were in attendance for this inspection:DEP - Aquatic Biologist Samantha Lutz, Aquatic Biologist Jessica McDuff and WQSS Brian Ayers.Trinity Mineral Partners - Kyle Miller, Brian Bennett and Todd Fantaskey (Northwest Soil Services)

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/04/2024
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8189889
Permit API: 065-25298
Unconventional: No
County: Jefferson
Municipality: Rose Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/04/2024
Comments: This site located in a grassy field west off Parks Road at the end of a short access, 320' west of residence and the spring used for their water supply. Well set-up for production with a separator, drip and 100 barrel tank in secondary containment. Annual electronic production report submitted through 2023. Will Warful reported on 5/9/2024 that the nipple on the holding tank rotted and leaked the contents of the 100 barrel holding tank into the unlined secondary containment. A vac truck was used to remove the water that remained in the secondary containment. At this inspection more contaminated material was removed from area where the tank was located in secondary containment, part of secondary containment embankment and ~50' northwest of the original release area. Water in the hole excavated northwest of the secondary containment was tested with handheld conductivity meter, the reading was over 4 milli Siemens. Water pooled in the hole where the secondary containment was excavated was ~2 milli siemens. You are hereby requested to continue to follow Department Policy 800-5000-001, Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil and Gas Well Sites or Access Road. This Policy sets forth the procedures that should be followed to resolve the violations associated with the spill/discharge/release noted in this Notice of Violation by using either the Act 2 or the Alternative Remediation Process.

Comments: On 1/6/23 a routine complete inspection of the Boord 7 OG Well site was conducted. During the inspection the following was observed:-An Act 9 sign was present at the site entrance (Photo #1).-A well tag was observed on the wellhead (Photo #2). -The well, production equipment, and production tank appeared to be in generally good condition (Photos #3-6).-The level of fluid in the secondary containment was over half-way full. The water exhibited elevated conductivity (Photos #6-7).-The containment did not appear to be leaking. A wetland adjacent to the containment did not exhibit elevated conductivity (Photo #8).I called Brian Goletz of Diversified and informed him of my findings. He stated that he would have a truck sent out to vacuum the containment. I informed Mr. Goletz that the water would have to be treated as waste due to the elevated conductivity. Violation of OGA3218.2(D) is being issued because the containment did not meet the 110% capacity at the time of the inspection. Violation of 78a64a(e)__is being issued for failure to remove stormwater prior to the capacity of the containment being reduced by 10% or more. Violation of 78a64a(f) is being issued for failure to remove a regulated substance that escaped primary containment.

Comments: In an effort to prevent the spread of the COVID-19 virus, the Department has conducted this administrative inspection in response to information provided by Chief. Based on the analytical results for isotopic samples collected by Chief at the above-referenced well on 6/17/2019 and 11/15/2019, methane was detected as follows: 48.11 % Methane detected at the Intermediate (9 5/8¿) x Surface (13 3/8¿) casing annulus on 6/17/2019. 3.79 % Methane detected at the Surface casing (13 3/8¿) x Conductor (20¿) annulus on 11/15/2019. 55.84 % Methane detected at the Intermediate (9 5/8¿) x Surface (13 3/8¿) casing annulus on 11/15/2019. 95.44 % Methane detected at the Production (5 ½") x Intermediate (9 5/8¿) casing annulus on 11/15/2019. The presence of methane at the Surface casing (13 3/8¿) x Conductor (20¿) is evidence of defective cement with methane outside of the surface casing string. As a result, violations of 25 Pa. Code §78a.73(b), §78a81(a)(2) and (3), and §78a.85(a)(5) have been cited. Please note that because your company provided a self-reported notification, no violation was cited for 25 Pa. Code §78a.86, defective cement, for the other annuli where methane was detected. However, Chief is required to comply with the Department¿s regulations, 25 Pa. Code §78a.86, which provides: ¿In a well that has defective, insufficient or improperly cemented casing, the operator shall report the defect to the Department within 24 hours of discovery by the operator and shall correct the defect. The operator shall correct the defect or submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days. If the defect cannot be corrected or an alternate method is not approved by the Department, the well shall be plugged under § 78a.91 ¿ 78a.98 (related to plugging).¿ Therefore, please provide a written response within 30 days of receipt of this Notice of Violation, as to when and how the above listed violations were or will be corrected, and what steps are being taken to prevent their recurrence.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2/14/2024 to K PETROLEUM INC in West Bethlehem Township, Washington county. 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8175801
Permit API: 125-22448
Unconventional: No
County: Washington
Municipality: West Bethlehem Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2/14/2024
Comments: On 02/14/2024, a routine complete inspection was conducted at the Hixenbaugh 1-P060 well. I notified Joel Greco of KPI ("operator"), regarding my findings on 02/14/2024. It was noted that there was rig work recently conducted onsite and that there were some things to address/clean up. The following was observed during the inspection:Well tags displaying the well and operators information were noted on site (Photos 1, 2).A methanol drum was noted on site. Although not required, I recommended placing containers within secondary containment to avoid substances from reaching the ground. Mr. Greco noted that the drum was empty and used for tubing that was experiencing freezing/thawing issues. I recommend that any unnecessary material is removed from the site and disposed of properly (Photos 3-5). In a 06/16/2017 compliance evaluation inspection (Inspection Report 2614040), a methanol drum was noted onsite without secondary containment and a violation of 91.34(a) was issued on 09/20/2016 (Inspection Report 2532594, Enforcement 348270).There was a spot of grease-like material on the ground near the tubing. The area is relatively small, however, I recommend that this is remediated and disposed of at an approved waste facility (Photos 4, 5). A section of grease-like material was noted along the tarp beside the oil tank. Although not required, secondary containment is recommended to be used to avoid any substances from reaching the ground (Photos 6-8). The operator explained that maintenance was being performed on the compressor station. Oil/grease material was noted within the trough along the compressor (Photos 9, 10). A grease-like material was noted around the wellhead. The wellhead and production equipment were in generally good condition. A splattered substance was noted on the production equipment; however, this may be paint. Monitoring recommended (Photos 11-13).The earthen berm around the production tank was in generally good condition and vegetated. Possible third-party disturbance and activity were noted near the production tank (Photos 14, 15). Several spots around the base of the production tanks displayed a grease/oil-like material on the tank and the ground. Petroleum crude oil noted on tanks right to know label. I recommend the removal of this material from the ground and cleaning off the tank. I also recommend lifting the tank to ensure no material is underneath. Marks from a material moving down the side of the tank were noted, most likely from precipitation (Photos 16-20). Violations were noted at this site on 09/20/2016 (Inspection Report 2532594, Enforcement 348270) regarding oil/grease within the earthen berm around the production tank. The access road was in relatively okay condition. No active E and S issues were noted; however, this road may be prone to accelerated erosion. I recommend routine maintenance of the access road (Photos 21-23). Several areas around the site displayed oil/grease on the ground. I recommend that each area be addressed, and the waste delivered to an approved waste facility. The Department is requesting that a waste manifest be submitted as soon as possible. Due to the discovery of grease/oil on the ground, violations of 78.54, SWMA 301, 91.34(a) are being issued.
